Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

excess noun

also excesses, in excess, to excess, nothing in excess, excessive, overindulgence, immoderation, immoderate

classical

Cic. Off. 1.89: mediocritātem illam tenēbit, quae est inter nimium et parum (Lewis & Short, s.v. nimius)
Plin. NH 33 prooem. 5 (Lewis & Short)

nimium, nimiī n.

noun, second declension

too much, excess

The neuter of nimius as a noun, with a genitive: aurī argentīque nimium, too much gold and silver. Proverbially nē quid nimis, “nothing in excess” (Ter. And. 61). For “too, too much” as an adverb, see too-excessively.

Other words

  • intemperantia, intemperantiae f. — excess, lack of self-control

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.22: omnium perturbātiōnum fontem esse dīcunt intemperantiam (Lewis & Short); Liv. 44.30: intemperantia vīnī (Lewis & Short)

    Excess in conduct: in eating, drinking, desire, speech (linguae, Tac. Ann. 4.18). Also arrogance towards others.

  • immoderātiō, immoderātiōnis f. — want of moderation, excess

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sull. 30: efferrī immoderātiōne verbōrum (Lewis & Short); Traupman 154

    Rare (Lewis & Short); the adjective immoderātus and Traupman’s immodicus (excessive, Traupman 152) are commoner.

  • immodicus, immodica, immodicum — immoderate, excessive

    adjective; in what: genitive or ablative, declension · also used · classical · Ov. M. 6.673 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 152, 154; Traupman 311

    (perhaps not before Augustus (Lewis & Short))

Examples

  • apprīmē in vītā esse ūtile ut nē quid nimis

    that the most useful thing in life is nothing in excessTer. And. 61

  • mediocritātem illam tenēbit, quae est inter nimium et parum

    he will keep to that mean which lies between too much and too littleCic. Off. 1.89 (Lewis & Short)

See also too, enough, too little, that’s enough!.
